content: Former bailiff of Stratford (1568) and glover on Henley Street
Carries small shop debts in Stratford
He counts three to the inch too few, smells a duchess, and does not punish the child who walks like him.
He will tell a debt cheerfully and smaller than it is, and he will show the pattern once.
He will name the bailiff's man and still refuse the thanks. Half a catch is as far as the song went.
He will call the walk a beggar's homecoming, and he will still sit down to the rye.
He will answer a sermon at his own table, stop a hand on a belt, and direct a street from the fourth rung.
A fairy in the doorway is as near as he comes to the five pounds.
He can make a barn and a spine into a blessing, and let the table take it as a jest.
